details:
Lunaspis is an interactive 3D space education project developed by Team Interfellas. It helps learners explore space science through simulated missions and teamwork. The project is intended for children aged seven and above, students, teachers, and adults interested in space.

How it works

Lunaspis supports up to six players in a shared mission. Players take different roles, including Flight Director, Ground Systems, Commander, Flight Engineer, Science Officer, and Space Specialist. Each role contributes to the mission through different tasks and decisions.

Players can launch a space shuttle, monitor flight information from Earth Control, dock with the International Space Station, and work together on science and engineering activities. They can also explore an Artemis-inspired lunar mission, design a CubeSat, and plan a BioNutrients-2-inspired experiment.

In the planet expedition activity, the Space Specialist selects a planet on the Solar Map, plans a spacecraft burn, and requests a trajectory forecast using NASA’s General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT). Other crew members can follow the shared mission progress.

NASA resources and technology

Our educational scenarios draw on NASA BioNutrients-2 information and CubeSat concepts. GMAT is used to calculate spacecraft trajectory forecasts when it is configured on the server. These missions use simplified training scenarios; their results are educational estimates, not live NASA flight data.

Development tools

We built Lunaspis with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Three.js creates the interactive 3D environments, while Node.js, Express, and Socket.IO support the server and multiplayer experience. AI-assisted tools supported parts of development, debugging, testing, and documentation.

Intended impact

Space science can be difficult to understand through text alone. Lunaspis makes abstract ideas more approachable by allowing users to explore visual environments, make decisions, and see the results of their choices. Through shared missions, we aim to encourage curiosity, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving.
